claim.pdf_says: Format 1 (boolean) is printed as ONE brace pair spanning both rows:  ⎧  B"[boolean-character-1]  ... "   ⎫ / ⎩  B'[boolean-character-1]  ... '   ⎭ ; Format 2 (hexadecimal-boolean) likewise as ONE brace pair spanning  BX"[hexadecimal-digit-1]  ... "  and  BX'[hexadecimal-digit-1]  ... ' .
claim.why_it_matters: The printed figure is a single brace enclosing two stacked alternatives, i.e. exactly one of the two rows is chosen (5.2.6.4). The markdown gives each row its OWN brace pair, so the figure reads as two independent required groups rather than one two-way choice. It also breaks the transcription's own established convention: the structurally identical alphanumeric-literal figures in 8.3.3.2.2 on page 137 are correctly rendered with the spanning-brace glyphs ⎧ ⎫ / ⎩ ⎭. Verified by zooming the rendered page: the braces carry no vertical choice-indicator bars, so the only defect is the split of the spanning brace.

verdict.reasoning:
Attempted refutation on every available ground and all of them failed.

1) Quotation accuracy — both sides quoted correctly. Rendered specs/ISO_COBOL.md page 140 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v140/spec_p140.png) and read the transcription slice directly out of specs/ISO_COBOL.md (not just the extracted work unit). §8.3.3.4.2 in the markdown contains exactly the four lines quoted, byte-for-byte, in two fenced blocks.

2) Printed glyphs — I looked at them myself rather than trusting the claim. Cropped the two figure regions and upscaled 3x (fmt1_zoom.png, fmt2_zoom.png). Each format shows exactly ONE left brace: a single tall '{' whose top arm sits above the first text row, whose central cusp lands in the inter-row gutter, and whose bottom arm descends below the second text row. Symmetrically ONE tall '}' on the right. There is no second brace glyph on either row, and no per-row brace baseline. I specifically checked for vertical choice-indicator bars (§5.2.6.4) between the braces and the text: there are none — the vertical strokes visible are the brace arms themselves, continuous from row 1 to row 2. So the figure is one two-way alternative group, nothing more.

3) Formatting-only / reflow defence — does not apply. This is not wrapping, hyphenation, or page-break furniture; it is a change in the number of grouping delimiters, which is the semantic payload of a COBOL general format.

4) 'Maybe two stacked { } lines still read as one choice' — rejected. Per §5.2.6.3, a brace pair encloses a portion of a general format of which one alternative shall be specified. Two consecutive complete brace groups is the notation for two successive mandatory elements, so the markdown as written literally reads 'specify B"..." and then also specify B'...'' — an impossible and wrong syntax. The printed figure means 'specify exactly one of the two quote forms'. The meaning genuinely changes.

5) Convention defence ('maybe the transcription just uses { } for all such figures') — decisively rejected by a document-wide scan. The spanning-brace glyph U+23A7 (⎧) occurs 455 times in specs/ISO_COBOL.md, including the structurally identical alphanumeric-literal figures at §8.3.3.2.2 on page 137, which are rendered ⎧ ... ⎫ / ⎩ ... ⎭ exactly as the claim states. A regex for whole lines of the form '{ ... }' returns exactly 4 hits in the entire transcription — and they are precisely these four boolean-literal lines. Page 140 is the unique deviation, not an alternate house style.

Severity 'structural' is correct: the defect changes the arity/grouping of a general format, which is the kind of figure a parser implementation is written from.
verdict.corrected_description: CONFIRMED as described, with one citation correction. The printed §8.3.3.4.2 boolean-literal general formats each use a single brace pair spanning both stacked rows (Format 1: B"..." over B'...'; Format 2: BX"..." over BX'...'), with no choice-indicator bars. The transcription splits each spanning brace into a per-row '{ ... }' pair, converting one two-way alternative into two independently mandatory groups. The governing clause for brace semantics is §5.2.6.3 (Braces), not §5.2.6.4 — §5.2.6.4 is Choice indicators (the '|' bars), which is the correct citation only for the secondary observation that no bars are present. Fix: render both figures with the transcription's own established spanning-brace glyphs, i.e. '⎧  B"[boolean-character-1]  … "  ⎫' / '⎩  B'[boolean-character-1]  … '  ⎭' and likewise for the BX forms, matching §8.3.3.2.2 on page 137.
